review_reference: Owner decisions of 11 Nov 2026 for open sign-up on outreach. (final): (1) keep the one-time Health ID support check before an organiser's first campaign goes Active; (2) no per-organiser limits (anti-bot protection and the invitation pending cap stay); (3) registrations never linked to a Health ID kept 1 year, then redacted; (4) joint-controller terms and DPIA approved, terms version 2026-11-01; (5) an existing staff login may start an outreach group with the same login; (6) free. 0125 and 0126 are placeholder numbers, renumbered when they merge; they are built on #222 (0122, campaign admins), which this release carries and which is described after them. reviewed_by is empty until the owner signs this declaration. #222's own reference: Decision relayed by the user in chat on 2026-11-11, answering which rule Outreach campaign management should follow (ADR-045's open question): "Campaign admins only (Recommended)", option B. Any staff member allowed to write campaigns may create one and becomes its admin; only that campaign's own admins open or close it and add members, enforced in outreach-api and in the database. Numbered 0122 when written; 0122 is now taken by #223 (sign-up fields), so it takes the next free number when it merges (the owner names it). reviewed_by is empty until the owner signs this declaration.
evidence: Migrations 0125_outreach_organisers.sql and 0126_outreach_retention.sql (with #222's 0122 before them) and services/ehr-api/database/runtime-grants.sql; unsigned until the owner signs (reviewed_by is empty). 0125 WHAT IT DOES: two roles, outreach_organiser (outreach.campaign.read/write, outreach.registration.read/write) and outreach_volunteer (outreach.campaign.read, outreach.registration.read/write); identity.outreach_organisations (one row per outreach group: its own organization and facility, lifecycle verified; review_state pending|reviewed|suspended), identity.outreach_organiser_signups and identity.outreach_invitations (forced RLS, no runtime privilege); public sign-up commands for the Identity runtime (system:auth: start, resend code, verify email, activate; the control outreach_organiser_signup_enabled, seeded OFF, gates them; an email that already has a login is answered email_registered; the public application quota per network and at most 5 sign-ups per network a day); identity.activate_outreach_organiser_for_account (a signed-in staff login starts its own group: a second membership as outreach_organiser at the new group, hospital roles untouched); a login with no staff record and no platform role (a patient's Health ID login) gets the answer 'patient_login' from the public sign-up, this command and every invitation path, so the screens can say plainly that a patient login cannot run or help an outreach group yet; the fence trigger account_roles_outreach_fence on auth.account_roles (only the two outreach roles at an outreach group, those roles nowhere else, nothing at a suspended group; revocations pass); outreach invitations (only an organiser invites, always outreach_volunteer, at most 50 pending; hospital staff invitations untouched); the trigger outreach_organiser_tenant_rules on outreach.registration_cases, campaigns, campaign_members and patient_mappings, acting only at an outreach group's facility (a registration needs a campaign, notes at most 280 characters, no campaign goes Active before support's review, nothing changes while suspended, no Health ID link); outreach.registration_consents (one immutable consent row per registration, guardian name required under 18; a deferred constraint trigger refuses a group's registration without one; a restrictive read policy shows a consent row only when its registration is visible to the caller, so a group member outside the campaign sees none); the permissive policy outreach_campaigns_member_lock so a campaign's own member who may register can lock it FOR SHARE (WITH CHECK false, so an UPDATE still needs outreach.campaign.write and an admin, 0122's trigger); support commands (list, one-click review with optional rename, suspend which revokes the group's roles and pending invitations, close a group's campaign, appoint a campaign admin; platform.admin.access with platform.facility.read, or .manage and .unlock to change; audited as platform actions). Support's campaign rescue runs inside a 'support run' (outreach.privileged_runs, a row for the current transaction that only these commands write); 0125 adds support policies on outreach.campaigns and outreach.campaign_members, lets 0122's two restrictive member policies pass inside a support run, and replaces outreach.validate_campaign_write() (0122's body, md5 7d6caf5f570aa38e8d33c63b27d9282c, kept whole after a first branch: inside a support run only the status may change, to closed). REPLACES platform.control_enabled (0086's body, md5 ed17b9d8097417363c0a6343e52aa47f, plus the new key) and the control key CHECK (0086's ten keys plus the new one). 0126 WHAT IT DOES: outreach.campaigns.closed_at (nullable, metadata-only ADD COLUMN), stamped by a trigger, never written by a caller; outreach.registration_retain_until = closed_at + 365 days (or last change + 365 days for a campaign closed before 0126), or starts_at + 365 days while not closed; outreach.registration_redactions; identity.sweep_expired_outreach_registrations(limit) (Identity runtime, system:auth) and identity.admin_redact_outreach_registration(case, reason) (support, on request): an outreach group's unlinked registration is redacted (full_name '[redacted]', phone and notes null, consent guardian '[redacted]', idempotency request hash zeroed; sex, age, campaign, dates kept) inside a 'retention run'; the sweeper also deletes sign-ups never activated after 30 days. Neither is executable by the Outreach runtime. REPLACES outreach.validate_registration_case_write() (0024, md5 a12d2b2573c5c7e52bcb5a8cdb1ec190; every rule kept, plus the redaction transition inside a retention run), outreach.validate_registration_campaign_write() (0110, md5 69469315f04554d2639dfa9f83591d4d; unchanged except that a redaction needs no membership) and the no-mutation trigger on outreach.command_idempotency (now refuses everything but the redaction of request_sha256); adds retention policies and lets 0045's two restrictive registration policies pass inside a retention run. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: nothing changes for hospitals, laboratories, pharmacies or the demo tenant (every new rule acts only at an outreach group's facility, and none exists until the control is switched on or the signed-in command runs); today's identity-api and outreach-api images work unchanged (no column they read changes; campaigns gains a nullable column). The control ships OFF. RELEASE ORDER: owner signs; apply 0122, 0125, 0126 (one release); release outreach-api and identity-api (PR-3, PR-4); website; switch the control on. PROVED on a throwaway local PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster (created and deleted; fictional data only): (1) production shape, every migration applied by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator with MIGRATION_TARGET=rds, baseline 0001-0122 with its role bootstrap, then 0125 and 0126 applied by the migrator alone: 85 of 86 SQL suites pass, and the one failure (database/tests/schema.integration.sql, ocr.job_events row-level security at line 1176) fails identically on the 0122 baseline without these migrations; (2) fresh install as the acceptance runner does it (superuser migrator, dry run, migrate, role bootstrap, verify-roles, plan 0 pending): all 86 SQL suites pass. New suites: services/ehr-api/test/database/outreach-organiser-signup.integration.sql (94 cases) and outreach-retention.integration.sql (25 cases), run as hid_identity_api_runtime and hid_outreach_api_runtime under the sessions those services set, and the fence cases as the owner of auth.account_roles. Changed suites: provider-self-service-control and provider-self-service-rollback (eleven control keys), order-routes-cannot-complete (control_enabled's new md5 1d24fbded6edff32d934d319b0135fb2), outreach-campaign-registration (0126's trigger md5 d995ccda598e41bf3edcffbafda38ddc; the lent owner also needs EXECUTE on outreach.privileged_run_active and registration_campaign_member), runtime-command-privileges (Case 4 accepts outreach_volunteer through the member-lock policy). #222 (0122) as declared there: Single migration 0122_outreach_campaign_admins.sql, unsigned until the owner signs (reviewed_by is empty). WHAT IT DOES: (1) CREATE OR REPLACE of outreach.validate_campaign_write() (0077's body, md5 1ac1e424e645378ab6e88a45542fccf9, kept whole) adding, on UPDATE, that the session's membership is an admin member of the campaign, else 42501 'Outreach campaign admin is required'; owner, SECURITY DEFINER and search_path unchanged; a row lock fires no trigger, so 0045's FOR SHARE on registration is unaffected. (2) Two RESTRICTIVE policies on outreach.campaign_members: insert only by an admin member of the campaign, or by its creator seeding themself as the first admin of a campaign with no member; delete only by an admin member. 0038's permissive policies stay. (3) outreach.campaign_staff(uuid) RETURNS TABLE(membership_id uuid, display_name text, campaign_role text), plpgsql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, platform, auth, identity, outreach, owned by outreach.campaigns' owner, EXECUTE for hid_outreach_runtime only: to a member of the campaign holding outreach.campaign.read at the session facility, its members (identity.staff.full_name and campaign role); to its admins also every active staff membership at the facility (campaign role null); anyone else no row; at most 1000 rows. No table, column, constraint, index, role or other function changes; no row read or written. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: today's identity-api refuses outreach.campaign.write, so no API path reaches a campaign write; campaign reads and registrations are unchanged. RELEASE ORDER: the owner signs this; apply 0122; release outreach-api; release identity-api last (it is what accepts outreach.campaign.write).
